title: Find the lexicographically largest string from the box i
spec:
You are given a string word, and an integer numFriends.
Alice is organizing a game for her numFriends friends. There are multiple rounds in the game, where in each round:

word is split into numFriends non-empty strings, such that no previous round has had the exact same split.
All the split words are put into a box.

Find the lexicographically largest string from the box after all the rounds are finished.

Example 1:

Input: word = "dbca", numFriends = 2
Output: "dbc"
Explanation:
All possible splits are:

"d" and "bca".
"db" and "ca".
"dbc" and "a".

Example 2:

Input: word = "gggg", numFriends = 4
Output: "g"
Explanation:
The only possible split is: "g", "g", "g", and "g".

Constraints:

1 <= word.length <= 5 * 10^3
word consists only of lowercase English letters.
1 <= numFriends <= word.length

bugs.description: Missing the numFriends == 1 case, where the whole word is the only piece.
Compares only first characters, ignoring ties among starting letters.
Only considers full-length windows, ignoring shorter suffixes at the end.
When every friend gets one letter, returns the first letter instead of the largest.
Never tries the last character as a start position.
Shortcut for two friends assumes the largest suffix is the longest one.
Only tries start positions below the piece size, confusing the piece length with the number of starts.
Window loop stops too early, considering only one shorter suffix at the end.
